sources.title: Football Manager 2023 — Recruitment Revamp (30 September 2022)
sources.observed: The official article describes role-based squad planning, future-season options, recruitment criteria and explicit scouting-completion states. The site's current FM26 chrome does not change the article's FM23 subject.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: separate role assignment, candidate search and knowledge evaluation into different working views.
sources.avoid: Do not import soccer positions, staff automation or multi-year planning mechanics that PAWA has not implemented.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer feature article opened and read; documented workflow, not hands-on usability evidence.

sources.title: Out of the Park Baseball 19 — Lineups manual
sources.observed: The manual separates the available-player list, batting order and positional depth chart. It documents distinct lineup scenarios and filtering/view controls.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: batting order and field assignments need different spatial treatments; browsing ratings need not always show the lineup.
sources.avoid: Do not copy OOTP's many nested panes, professional roster assumptions or unsupported platoon/DH scenarios.
sources.evidenceType: Official versioned manual opened and read; historical workflow reference, not a claim about current OOTP.

sources.title: EA SPORTS College Football 25 — Dynasty Deep Dive
sources.observed: The developer article documents a recruit board with actionable status, a separate position-needs view, progressive scouting disclosure, staged recruiting and a school-strengths view. It describes finite weekly recruiting resources and coach abilities with prerequisites.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: expose the specific scarce resource beside the next action and make uncertainty, need and phase visible without repeating every detail.
sources.avoid: Do not transplant football scholarship counts, stages, attribute ranges, recruiting hours, coach rules or transfer guarantees into PAWA.
sources.evidenceType: Official producer/game-designer deep dive opened and read; documented interface/workflow. No game execution or independent enjoyment test.

sources.title: Football Manager 2023 — Dynamic Manager Timeline (30 September 2022)
sources.observed: The official article describes chronological career moments with extra emphasis on major achievements and includes setbacks rather than only trophies.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: program, coach and rivalry history should use factual chronology; a completed class can become a keepsake rather than another management dashboard.
sources.avoid: Do not invent event significance scores, unsupported sharing or historical events that PAWA never stored.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer feature article opened and read; narrative-structure reference, not proof of PAWA archive completeness.

sources.title: College Football 26 — Dynasty & Team Builder Deep Dive
sources.observed: EA describes team needs pinned above the prospect list, consistent attribute ordering for comparisons, board trend indicators and favorites. The article explains why these reduce switching between views.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: place positional need beside the target board, keep comparable scouting attributes aligned, and expose a concise next-action state using only known information.
sources.avoid: Do not import football positions, recruiting-hour costs, abilities or success probabilities into PAWA. A cleaner interface does not authorize new rules.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer article opened September 18, 2026; described interaction and image captions, not hands-on validation.

sources.title: OOTP 6.5 official screenshot gallery — schedule, box score and roster
sources.observed: Historical gallery captions describe a daily schedule with probable starters, links to completed box scores/game logs, and player names linking to profiles. This is documentation of workflow; no current-edition or hands-on usability claim.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: keep fixture identity continuous across preparation, reporting and inspection; make performance rows lead to the actual player.
sources.avoid: Do not copy legacy desktop density or imply that an external Power Pros game supplies a game log.
sources.evidenceType: Official historical screenshot-gallery captions; opened 2026-09-18; visual geometry not independently measured.

sources.title: OOTP 12 official manual — Commissioner Portal
sources.observed: The manual separates commissioner actions, reports and tools. Team export checks include current-date status. Its automator can stop for missing exports and produces an operation-status log.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: make readiness and blockers actionable, distinguish them from presence, and show server operation outcomes alongside recovery restrictions.
sources.avoid: Do not transfer FTP mechanics, automatic file exchange, or one-click advance guarantees into PAWA.
sources.evidenceType: Official historical manual workflow description; opened 2026-09-18; no runtime evaluation.

sources.title: MLB The Show 24 official manual — More Ways to Play
sources.observed: The manual treats Postseason as a bracket-oriented mode and Custom Leagues as configurable season competition with friends. It does not document PAWA-style external-result approvals.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: let tournament structure dominate postseason; reserve celebratory framing for a verified championship.
sources.avoid: Do not import MLB bracket rules, assume feature parity, or call pending companion reports official.
sources.evidenceType: Official edition-specific manual; opened 2026-09-18; workflow reference only.

sources.title: NBA 2K11 official PC manual — Main Menu, printed page 13
sources.observed: The publisher manual, distributed on Steam CDN, distinguishes roster-management tools, sharing created content, and saving/loading files. Its historical online features are not evidence of present service availability.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: explicitly separate reusable roster/class files, public previews and mutations of an active league.
sources.avoid: Do not imply 2K compatibility, current 2K service support, automatic console upload, or a new marketplace.
sources.evidenceType: Primary publisher PDF; page 13 text read on 2026-09-18; menu semantics, not a contemporary visual reference.

sources.title: Football Manager 26 — Reimagined User Interface
sources.observed: The developer describes overview-to-detail interaction, task/message filters, an action panel, upcoming fixtures and a two-week calendar. It explicitly discusses readable type, contrast and platform-specific adaptation.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: surface the decision and its context first, use compact drill-down deliberately, and retain meaningful screen-specific structures.
sources.avoid: Do not turn every PAWA screen into tiles or treat developer marketing as proof of usability.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer feature explanation; opened 2026-09-18; no hands-on or comparative usability test.

sources.title: OOTP official wiki — Creating Games
sources.observed: The official manual separates standard, custom, historical, advanced and quick-start creation paths. It describes a wizard for custom setup and identifies advanced mode as a separate route.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: make the mode decision explicit, then expose only the settings relevant to that mode; end on a review sheet.
sources.avoid: Do not import OOTP's MLB modes, historical database or automatic management systems into PAWA.
sources.evidenceType: Official manual text opened 2026-09-18; documented workflow, not a hands-on test.

sources.title: Football Manager 26 — Reimagined User Interface
sources.observed: FM describes a Portal combining home and inbox, task/unread filters, an action panel, grouped top navigation, and bookmarks. Tiles open more detailed cards. The article says readability and platform-specific screens shaped the redesign.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: separate actionable messages from unread messages; reveal secondary detail on demand; give the game menu named destination groups.
sources.avoid: Do not copy the universal tile system. PAWA needs distinct page composition rather than the same cards everywhere.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer feature text opened 2026-09-18; claims describe design intent, not proof of usability.

sources.title: OOTP official wiki — History Index
sources.observed: The history index begins with seasons and finalists, emphasizes the champion, and links years to team history. Separate destinations cover players, teams, managers, leaderboards, awards and accomplishments.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: use stable year/category coordinates and evidence links so archive exploration cannot be confused with the live league.
sources.avoid: Do not copy the full nested link hierarchy or assume historical information exists when PAWA snapshots lack it.
sources.evidenceType: Official manual text opened 2026-09-18; information architecture evidence, not a current in-game screenshot audit.

sources.title: NBA 2K25 — MyNBA and MyGM Courtside Report
sources.observed: 2K describes fewer, more consequential MyGM conversations; historical news presentation changes from newspaper to web formats and social feeds. The report also describes simplifying staff management.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: make weekly news an editorial issue, live activity a compact stream, and narrative decisions a focused scene. Different content deserves different reading rhythm.
sources.avoid: Do not add walkable offices, invented NPC conversations, era simulation or unsupported role-playing effects.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer report opened 2026-09-18; documented content and presentation patterns, not hands-on validation.

sources.title: EA College Football 26 — Dynasty and Team Builder Deep Dive
sources.observed: EA describes choosing an existing coach or creating one. Its Trophy Room records achievements with season, team, score or individual recipient context; selecting a trophy exposes more information.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: coach setup should foreground identity and supported tradeoffs; awards should present recipients with the actual season and achievement evidence.
sources.avoid: Do not borrow licensed marks, imply PAWA has EA's coach progression, or turn every statistical record into a trophy.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer article and accompanying image descriptions opened 2026-09-18; no game session or video playthrough.

screens.composition: One campus vista fills the frame; a narrow vertical play menu sits in intentional empty sky/dugout space. Last accessible dynasty is a single subtitle under Continue.
screens.primaryDecision: Resume a specific dynasty or begin another journey.
screens.interaction: Arrow keys and pointer choose menu items; Continue names its target before navigation.
screens.compact: Keep the vertical menu over a quiet solid-backed crop; account control stays at top.
screens.difference: An atmospheric entry with four destinations, not a working league dashboard.
unapprovedDependencies: Final campus key art; no animated environment or controller support implied.
screens.title: Title screen

screens.composition: A single compact credential sheet floats over a muted entrance crop. Show the intended league destination above the form.
screens.primaryDecision: Sign in and return to the intended destination.
remove: Account marketing and duplicate sign-in controls
screens.interaction: Submit once; retain non-secret identity input on failure; route only after confirmed success.
screens.compact: Full-width form, visible Back, keyboard-safe spacing; no side panels.
screens.difference: A short authentication task rather than a game menu.
screens.title: Sign in

screens.composition: One linear registration sheet uses three visual bands: account identity, credentials, and creation consequence. Invite context remains a small header.
screens.primaryDecision: Create the account required to own the requested session.
screens.interaction: Validate beside fields; preserve valid entries after rejection; creation is a single named action.
screens.compact: One column with text labels; errors precede the submit action.
screens.difference: Account creation stays distinct from coach customization.
screens.title: Create account

screens.composition: A short guest pass contains the real persistence limitation followed by two stacked choices. Avoid a second onboarding funnel.
screens.primaryDecision: Enter as a guest with known limits or create an account.
screens.interaction: The guest action begins one session request; warning remains visible while pending.
screens.compact: Two full-width labeled buttons below the consequence sentence.
screens.difference: A deliberate temporary-access fork; not another form.
screens.title: Guest entry

screens.composition: One full-width list of dynasty spines: name, team mark, mode, current phase and last activity. The last played entry is taller; each entry owns its Continue action. Tools live behind a labeled library command.
screens.primaryDecision: Choose which world to resume.
remove: KPI cards copied from the active league
screens.interaction: Choose a save directly; a contextual menu handles details/deletion separately from Continue.
screens.compact: Vertical save spines retain name, phase and primary action; no carousel.
screens.difference: A library of worlds with no need to open a generic inspector first.
screens.title: Dynasty selection

screens.composition: A full-width step sequence shows Mode, Competition, Sources and Review. One task owns the center at a time; completed decisions become a collapsible summary ribbon.
screens.primaryDecision: Create the exact reviewed simulation or companion world.
screens.interaction: Back preserves selections; choosing a mode reveals relevant supported fields; Create occurs only on the review step.
screens.compact: Single step with top Back/step label and readable next action, never four squeezed columns.
screens.difference: A narrowing decision sequence rather than a configurable dashboard.
unapprovedDependencies: Step draft persistence across reload requires implementation; do not promise it.
screens.title: New dynasty

screens.composition: Conference headings divide a full-width school ballot. Each row shows monogram, name, selected state and relevant eligibility. A top count explains required versus chosen teams.
screens.primaryDecision: Confirm a valid competition field.
screens.interaction: Toggle eligible schools; constraint feedback names the blocking rule; confirmation reviews totals.
screens.compact: Conference selector plus checked rows; selected count remains above the list.
screens.difference: A multi-select competition ballot, not scouting or team comparison.
screens.title: Competition selection

screens.composition: A large cel coach and selected school mark form a media-day backdrop; one focused foreground form progresses from school to identity to existing skill allocation.
screens.primaryDecision: Commit to the coach and school combination.
remove: Cosmetic controls that imply unsupported bonuses
screens.interaction: Preview permitted identity changes; claim/save only after confirming current availability and valid allocation.
screens.compact: Portrait becomes a compact header; each form stage uses full width.
screens.difference: Identity gets a character-creation moment rather than an admin record editor.
unapprovedDependencies: Production cel customization kit; no new archetypes, perks or appearance mechanics.
screens.title: Coach and school setup

screens.composition: A prominent league masthead leads into school/coach seat rows. A separate readiness strip summarizes class, schedule and assignments. The commissioner Start action follows its exact blockers.
screens.primaryDecision: Claim an available school or resolve the blocker preventing league start.
remove: Decorative scene above all useful content
screens.interaction: Selecting an open seat opens only its claim flow; start is role-aware and rechecks prerequisites.
screens.compact: Rollcall becomes stacked seat rows; readiness appears before the final start control.
screens.difference: A social readiness room with named occupants, not a general operations console.
unapprovedDependencies: Any presence display needs actual freshness data; no chat or synchronized avatar lobby.
screens.title: Dynasty lobby

screens.composition: A slim vertical stage timeline sits beside the reviewed creation name. Completed/current/failed stages have explicit text; the final successful state replaces progress with Enter dynasty.
screens.primaryDecision: Wait, enter the confirmed world, or follow the supported recovery path.
remove: Campus construction implying real facility progression
screens.interaction: Revisit the same operation identity after navigation; show retry only when supported.
screens.compact: One stage stack and one status action; details expand downward.
screens.difference: A receipt for one operation, not a loading dashboard.
unapprovedDependencies: Resumption/retry only if creation API supports it; no new recovery guarantee.
screens.title: Creating dynasty

screens.composition: A single invitation letter names the league, intended role if known, and current account. Acceptance and account switching are distinct actions below the identity check.
screens.primaryDecision: Join this league as the displayed account.
remove: Raw token displayed as decorative code
screens.interaction: Accept once; preserve invitation context across sign-in; an existing member gets Open league.
screens.compact: One readable letter with actions below; no league navigation until authorized.
screens.difference: A membership decision, not a miniature league home.
screens.title: League invitation

screens.composition: One broad next-game placard fills the left half; the right half is a short ranked to-do list. A thin latest-result strip sits beneath. League detail opens separately, not under eight dashboard modules.
screens.primaryDecision: What must I do before this week can progress?
keep: Next real game and mode-correct action
remove: Repeated budget summaries already visible in recruiting
screens.interaction: Select a task to enter its working screen; complete it and return to the same brief. Mark ready stays separate from advancing league.
screens.compact: At narrower widths, next game then task list; at most one recent-outcome row. No persistent inspector.
screens.difference: An agenda composition, not a table or profile screen.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Task prioritization must use existing phase/blocker data; no invented urgency or autonomous advance.
screens.title: Matchday brief

screens.composition: Full-width manifest with a generous identity column and just six default fields: name, position, year, B/T, OVR, status. A slim position filter sits above. A player profile opens only on demand; no mandatory right inspector.
screens.primaryDecision: Who can fill the role I need?
remove: Permanent hometown/portrait inspector stealing comparison width
screens.interaction: Choose Ratings, Batting or Pitching column preset; select row to open profile; return restores row and sort. Depth is a deliberate view change.
screens.compact: Name plus position/year/OVR in the list; remaining metric preset replaces columns rather than extends offscreen.
screens.difference: Maximum comparable rows and no decorative hero; visual priority is aligned numbers.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Column presets use only available data. Roster role response shape needs authenticated QA; no new edit permissions.
screens.title: Roster command

screens.composition: A schematic defensive diamond presents the team's actual positional shape. A compact rotation strip sits beneath, with record and next fixture in a narrow masthead. Roster and Schedule open dedicated views.
screens.primaryDecision: Where is this team strong or exposed?
remove: Full program-history wall on current-team overview
Three generic summary cards plus inspection rail
screens.interaction: Select a position to see its current options; selecting an athlete opens their read-only profile unless authorized. Formation diagram is navigational, not a claim about projected starters.
screens.compact: At compact size use named position slots in diamond order and a separate rotation tab; never shrink athlete labels to dots.
screens.difference: Spatial current-team overview; the program screen instead owns institutional history.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Must use actual assigned roles; missing assignments say unassigned. Any generated strength assessment needs a verified model.
screens.title: Team scouting dossier

screens.composition: Editorial yearbook cover at left: campus miniature, school crest, founding identity. A broad season timeline occupies the main canvas; selecting a season replaces it with that year's documented record. Facilities appears as a short factual caption.
screens.primaryDecision: What story has this program earned?
remove: Permanent scouting-style inspector and action-cost widgets
screens.interaction: Move through seasons or jump to honors; open archived evidence from a specific moment. Return retains the selected year.
screens.compact: Compact cover masthead then vertical chronology; no squeezed horizontal timeline.
screens.difference: A historical publication with breathing room, not another roster-management screen.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Needs stored season/event provenance. Do not invent campus history, achievements or export support.
screens.title: Program profile

screens.composition: Cel coach portrait and name anchor a vertical credential on the left. Career is a chronological record; Skills switches the main canvas to the actual perk structure. Settings is a quiet form, not a profile card collage.
screens.primaryDecision: What defines this coach, and which eligible improvement matters next?
keep: Actual skill prerequisites and remaining points
remove: Every badge repeated as a separate large card
Private settings displayed in public career views
screens.interaction: Switch Career, Attributes, Skills, Strategy and Settings; selecting a perk previews actual cost/effect before eligible purchase.
screens.compact: Identity collapses to a slim header; one active chapter fills the display. Skills has a readable list equivalent.
screens.difference: A person-centered passport that changes working surface by chapter; it is not a scouting board.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No new archetypes, respec rules or XP mechanics. Controller tree navigation remains future implementation.
screens.title: Coach profile

screens.composition: Four labeled playbook dividers frame a single choice surface. The current selection and one candidate are shown as parallel text/diagram columns, with the actual consequence sentence directly between them.
screens.primaryDecision: Which existing philosophy should this program adopt?
screens.interaction: Choose offense, pitching, pitch or culture; preview one alternative; Apply only if allowed. Selecting a preview never saves.
screens.compact: One divider selector and two vertically paired descriptions; chosen state stays in the header.
screens.difference: A side-by-side choice workbench with no list of people or persistent inspector.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: All tradeoffs and phase restrictions must come from existing rules; changes are not approved by this research.
screens.title: Program identity

screens.composition: A large opposing-monogram composition carries the series record. Under it, a chronological sequence of verified meetings uses score and season as the visual rhythm. A compact selector changes the rival.
screens.primaryDecision: Which contest gives this rivalry its meaning?
remove: Manufactured feud copy or rivalry heat without data
screens.interaction: Select a meeting for its supported result; choose next matchup to prepare. History and next-game actions are visibly distinct.
screens.compact: Stack the two crests around the record; vertical match history below.
screens.difference: A matchup story, not a general program profile.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No invented rivalry causes or intensity changes; missing historical meetings remain unavailable.
screens.title: Coaching rivalries

screens.composition: One wide target ledger is the default: prospect, role, known quality, interest/stage, current commitment and next permitted action. A compact resource meter and needs shortcut sit in the command row. Selecting an action expands a shallow row tray, not a permanent profile column.
screens.primaryDecision: Where should the next recruiting action go?
remove: Full recruit biography beside every routine board action
screens.interaction: Sort/filter targets, expand a single action tray, review cost and act. Open dossier only for a deeper evaluation. Do not introduce batch spending.
screens.compact: Essential four-column board and named metric preset; an expanded tray uses the full row width. Top controls stay readable.
screens.difference: A resource-allocation ledger rather than a player-card gallery or three-panel dashboard.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No borrowed football recruiting hours or caps. Any priority sort must be factual/user-controlled; private ratings stay hidden.
screens.title: Recruiting desk

screens.composition: A media-day portrait and identity occupy one third; a structured scouting sheet uses the rest. Known traits, unknown traits and expressed priorities are visibly distinct. A compact competition ladder sits below the relevant recruiting chapter.
screens.primaryDecision: Do I know enough to pursue this athlete?
keep: Player priorities and team fit facts
remove: All attributes, biography and competition visible at once
Gem/bust styling that reveals private data
screens.interaction: Switch Scouting, Priorities and Recruitment chapters using the existing data sections; each explains its knowledge boundary. Primary action changes with eligibility.
screens.compact: Portrait becomes an identity strip; one sheet chapter at a time, with no nested tiny tabs.
screens.difference: A readable dossier for one person, deliberately slower and more reflective than the target ledger.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Do not invent scouting confidence ranges or reports. Warm copy cannot imply facts not stored.
screens.title: Recruit scouting profile

screens.composition: A position-needs strip heads a compact transfer candidate list. Each row foregrounds remaining eligibility, origin, known ability and availability. Comparing a candidate opens current-option versus candidate, not a general recruiting biography.
screens.primaryDecision: Does this transfer solve an immediate roster vacancy?
screens.interaction: Choose needed role, shortlist/inspect an eligible candidate, then review permitted offer. Existing roster option remains the comparison baseline.
screens.compact: Need selector, candidate list, then full-width comparison; no always-open inspector.
screens.difference: Immediate roster replacement workflow, visibly different from high-school relationship building.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No transfer guarantees, forecasts or NIL obligations beyond actual PAWA rules; unknown prior stats remain unknown.
screens.title: Transfer portal

screens.composition: A uniform cel contact sheet groups the class by actual position, with a compact count/needs ribbon above. Signed versus verbal status is printed on each athlete tile. Rankings is a separate comparison view.
screens.primaryDecision: Who is joining, and which needs remain?
keep: Position coverage and actual class ranking
remove: Another full-width dense board for a completed class
screens.interaction: Select athlete for profile; choose season/team explicitly; switch to Rankings without losing class selection.
screens.compact: Two-column contact sheet with stable card proportions; count and status remain text, never hidden icons.
screens.difference: A class portrait collection; density is lower because the job is recognition and review.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No arrival celebration for verbal-only commitments. Do not infer roster additions from presentation state.
screens.title: Committed class

screens.composition: Proposed single-athlete stage on miniature home diamond: nameplate movement resolves into arrival sports profile. A class contact strip only appears after the spotlight. The stage is not surrounded by management widgets.
screens.primaryDecision: Whose arrival should I spotlight, and when do I return to the class?
remove: Automatic repeated long reveal for every athlete
screens.interaction: Choose spotlight, play or skip, inspect final card, return to class. Reduced motion goes directly to readable arrival profile.
screens.compact: Full canvas portrait/nameplate composition; controls remain at top and readable before motion.
screens.difference: A ceremony with a clear beginning/end, unlike the static commits gallery.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Frisk's A D A A B A A C A B recipe remains unapproved. Assets, sound, scrapbook/export and timing require approval and implementation.
screens.title: Signing day and arrival ceremony

screens.composition: A league-wide register uses teams as compact rows and Graduation / Draft / Portal as count columns. Selecting a count expands the named athletes directly below that team. It is primarily a read-only overview.
screens.primaryDecision: Which programs are losing which players?
remove: One large player card per departure
Speculative returning-roster forecasts presented as facts
screens.interaction: Filter category or team, expand exact count, inspect athlete; open own departure workflow only when eligible.
screens.compact: Team name plus three labeled counts; expansion lists names/reasons; no hidden horizontal table travel.
screens.difference: An institutional count-and-drill register, not a personal decision queue.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Actual endpoint data is authoritative; any forecast/continuity view needs separately verified data.
screens.title: League departures overview

screens.composition: A short pending-player queue sits above a large consequence comparison: retain if permitted versus depart. Current and resulting roster count/budget use aligned labels. Finalized players move to a separate receipt view.
screens.primaryDecision: Is this eligible retention choice worth its actual cost?
remove: League-wide departure browser beside every decision
Celebratory or alarmist framing that biases the choice
screens.interaction: Inspect one case; choose a legal option; review irreversible scope before finalization. Queue selection never performs mutation.
screens.compact: One case per full panel with a numbered queue indicator; paired consequences stack without shrinking type.
screens.difference: A deliberate decision workspace, not a table with tiny destructive buttons.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Probabilities only if server supplies them; no invented retention guarantee, costs or projection.
screens.title: Departure decisions

screens.composition: Available athletes occupy a lean bid ledger, while a narrow permanent capacity/budget strip shows the real constraint. Cuts are a separate roster action sheet, never a column of tempting red buttons beside bids.
screens.primaryDecision: Which legal bid best fills a real vacancy?
remove: Full profile cards for every bidder
Cuts mixed into routine bid selection
screens.interaction: Select candidate, inspect relevant traits, enter bid, review available resources and submit; inspect results separately.
screens.compact: Bid list with named amount controls; selection opens one full-width bid tray. Capacity persists above.
screens.difference: A transaction board organized around offer amounts and limited space, not a recruiting relationship tracker.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No automatic bidding, market forecasts or assumed winning price; pending-obligation handling must match real rules.
screens.title: Cuts and walk-on bids

screens.composition: A horizontal week band above grouped home/away series; fixtures occupy most of the canvas. Selecting one expands its state-specific action inline, with a compact opponent strip.
screens.primaryDecision: Which fixture needs my next action?
keep: Explicit pending, disputed and accepted labels
Prepare / Report / Review / Result according to permission
remove: A large scoreboard that hides the next fixture
screens.interaction: Move week, filter team, then select a game; return preserves week and selection. Pending scores never receive a final-result treatment.
screens.compact: Use chronological day groups, not a compressed month grid; status text stays next to score.
screens.difference: Time and series grouping are the organizing structure; it must not resemble the commissioner blocker queue.
unapprovedDependencies: Explicit date/day grouping requires verified schedule fields; do not manufacture dates from week numbers.
screens.title: Season schedule

screens.composition: Away and home occupy opposing halves; central matchup metrics align on shared rows. The selected starter and own batting order sit below their team, not in generic KPI cards.
screens.primaryDecision: What lineup or availability issue should I resolve before this game?
remove: Decorative stadium occupying the decision area
screens.interaction: Open a player from a matchup row or move to the existing lineup workflow. Companion mode explains that preparation does not send changes into Power Pros.
screens.compact: Render paired metric rows above one full-width lineup chapter; never squeeze two roster tables.
screens.difference: This is a pregame comparison surface, while report is an entry workspace and box-score is a completed record.
unapprovedDependencies: Any new matchup calculation, export packet or lineup-writing control needs separate approval and backend evidence.
screens.title: Game preparation

screens.composition: Persistent matchup and report-state strip; a wide entry sheet with team/stat selectors; a collapsible source-image lane and adjacent field-level errors; final review is a distinct summary stage.
screens.primaryDecision: Is the played result accurate enough to submit for review?
keep: OCR uncertainty and server validation beside the affected field
remove: Notebook decoration that reduces entry width
screens.interaction: Keyboard entry follows baseball columns; error selection focuses its cell. Submit shows pending review only after server confirmation; stale revision preserves the local draft for reconciliation.
screens.compact: One team and stat group per view; source preview toggles without losing entry position; review stays reachable at top.
screens.difference: The scorebook is editable and evidence-linked; its layout must differ visibly from both a read-only result and an approval decision.
unapprovedDependencies: Durable cross-device draft saving and new OCR capabilities are not approved by this layout.
screens.title: Report a Power Pros game

screens.composition: One compact unavailable notice beside the actual matchup identity; underneath, supported destinations only.
screens.primaryDecision: Where can I continue with this game?
keep: Return to schedule or accepted result
screens.interaction: Focus the supported return action; a missing/inaccessible game falls back to schedule without inventing identity.
screens.compact: Single panel with normal back control.
screens.difference: A short dead-end recovery surface; no dashboard, ceremony or simulated broadcast shell.
unapprovedDependencies: Playable pitch-by-pitch sessions remain a separate engineering gate.
screens.title: Play-by-play unavailable

screens.composition: Round columns dominate the canvas, with explicit stage titles and series state inside each node. A selected matchup opens detail below the bracket rather than replacing it with cards.
screens.primaryDecision: What is the next eligible matchup, and how does it affect the path?
remove: Generic schedule list as the only desktop tournament view
screens.interaction: Select a node to review game or series details; retain the visible parent and next round. No unsupported manual reseeding control.
screens.compact: Round selector with ordered matchups and explicit previous/next path labels.
screens.difference: Topology, not chronology or numeric tables, is the primary reading order.
unapprovedDependencies: Do not invent elimination formats, tie rules, bracket repair or qualification guarantees.
screens.title: Postseason hub

screens.composition: One verified champion identity and season headline, a restrained trophy composition, then a factual final-series strip and entry into the season record.
screens.primaryDecision: Celebrate this verified season or inspect its record?
screens.interaction: Skip ends presentation only; view record does not advance the league. Missing champion yields an unfinished-season state.
screens.compact: Single portrait composition with legible score strip and visible skip/back.
screens.difference: This is intentionally the emotional peak; administrative pages must not reuse its hero composition.
unapprovedDependencies: New trophies, team art, audio and ceremony animation require art/implementation approval.
screens.title: Championship presentation

screens.composition: A full-width statistical ledger gets a two-line control header: season/scope, then batting/pitching and metric preset. The leading row has restrained emphasis; player details open only on demand.
screens.primaryDecision: Which performance ranks highest under this scope and qualification?
remove: Decorative KPI totals repeating table columns
screens.interaction: Sorting changes the named order; choose a row for a full profile and return to the same sort/position.
screens.compact: Keep rank, athlete, selected metric and sample in view; switch metric groups instead of shrinking every column.
screens.difference: A comparison instrument that devotes nearly all width to aligned evidence.
screens.title: Statistics desk

screens.composition: A category index opens a typeset record page: value and holder first, then tied holders, team/year and source link. Single-season and career scope sit above the record list.
screens.primaryDecision: Which achievement and holder should I inspect?
screens.interaction: Open a record category, select the record, follow its archived evidence; Back retains category.
screens.compact: Category selector opens one record page with tied holders stacked.
screens.difference: An achievement reference book, distinct from sorting current-season statistics.
unapprovedDependencies: Do not infer all-time records from incomplete archives.
screens.title: Record book

screens.composition: A visible year index leads to a season contents page. The selected year is stamped across the masthead; chapters open full-width historical tables or spreads.
screens.primaryDecision: Which completed season and chapter do I want to revisit?
keep: Links to archived teams and fixtures
remove: All chapters simultaneously in dashboard cards
screens.interaction: Year first, chapter second; preserve both in navigation and clearly mark any link back to live data.
screens.compact: Year chooser and chapter list replace a permanent rail; one chapter owns the screen.
screens.difference: A historical container organized by year, not the live league page tinted sepia.
screens.title: Season archive

screens.composition: A single team-season masthead leads into a historical roster register with chapter switches for recorded results and honors. The year remains beside the team name everywhere.
screens.primaryDecision: Inspect this team as it existed in that year.
remove: Current roster silently filling snapshot gaps
screens.interaction: Historical players open a read-only snapshot view; Live team is a separately labeled exit.
screens.compact: One register section at a time; each detail keeps team and year at top.
screens.difference: A frozen team volume rather than a live profile with an archive badge.
screens.title: Archived team

screens.composition: One issue uses an editorial lead headline, compact result rail and two supporting columns of factual briefs. Required decisions appear in a clearly labeled box, not inside celebratory copy. Issue navigation is a top date chooser.
screens.primaryDecision: What materially changed this week, and what needs my attention?
screens.interaction: Read the issue in priority order; open a source or task without marking it resolved merely by reading.
screens.compact: One-column newspaper order: lead, decisions, results, supporting briefs.
screens.difference: A curated weekly edition, unlike the raw ticker or personal inbox.
unapprovedDependencies: Editorial prioritization must use available events; no fabricated quotes or generated facts.
screens.title: League news digest

screens.composition: A stationary chronological wire groups compact events by date/week. Category chips sit above the stream; new events collect behind a count button rather than moving existing rows.
screens.primaryDecision: Which recent event deserves inspection?
screens.interaction: Open event inline or follow its linked record; manually reveal newer items and retain reading position.
screens.compact: Single event column with filters in a named sheet; no sideways ticker.
screens.difference: A low-friction activity log rather than another editorial homepage.
unapprovedDependencies: New-event count requires supported polling/event updates; do not imply live sockets.
screens.title: League ticker

screens.composition: A narrow message queue shares the page with one full reading sheet. Two top filters independently distinguish unread from unresolved; any valid action lives at the end of the actual message.
screens.primaryDecision: Read or act on the selected coach message.
screens.interaction: Select message, read context, then follow its action. Archive remains a separate command and never resolves the underlying task.
screens.compact: Queue and reader become two screens; Back restores selection and filters.
screens.difference: A personal correspondence workflow; the only deliberate list-reader split in this group.
unapprovedDependencies: Unresolved filter requires reliable task-state linkage; otherwise keep supported categories.
screens.title: Coach inbox

screens.composition: One active arc opens as a story spread with a scene headline, factual context, participants and a small consequence timeline. Eligible choices/votes sit beneath the context. Intel and commissioner tools are separate chapters.
screens.primaryDecision: Choose a supported story action or vote with its known consequences.
remove: Invented dialogue or implied hidden rewards
screens.interaction: Read context before selecting a choice; confirmation names the option; expired/completed decisions become read-only history.
screens.compact: Context then choices then history; no side panel holding required information.
screens.difference: A focused narrative decision, not a news list with a vote widget.
unapprovedDependencies: New dialogue, branching outcomes or artwork require separate design approval; use existing story content.
screens.title: Storyline hub

screens.composition: An ordered queue of current blockers occupies the main area; phase/week and active operation anchor the header. Reports, records and settings are secondary destinations grouped by task.
screens.primaryDecision: What prevents the league from progressing safely?
remove: Equal-weight grid of every dangerous action
screens.interaction: Selecting a blocker opens its exact record; pending acceptance and absent reports have different actions. Advance remains governed by server preflight.
screens.compact: A task list first; selection becomes a full detail route/panel with back restoring queue position.
screens.difference: A work queue organized by obligation, unlike the team hub and the permanent audit ledger.
unapprovedDependencies: New priority scoring, presence telemetry or force-advance behavior is not implied.
screens.title: Commissioner office

screens.composition: League/team context fixed above a dense player grid; a selected row opens a focused category editor. Changes appear in a review band before the permitted save.
screens.primaryDecision: Which exact live player field am I correcting?
remove: Hero athlete card before the editable fields
screens.interaction: Search team/player, edit one category, then review changed values where existing APIs support it; rejected saves retain inputs.
screens.compact: Select player first, then a full-width category form; search state survives Back.
screens.difference: Live-league correction with narrow scope; reusable file authoring belongs in roster-library.
unapprovedDependencies: New bulk edits, undo guarantees and before/after persistence require dedicated validation.
screens.title: Commissioner roster editor

screens.composition: Class identity and filters above a prospect table; selected recruit expands attribute groups, with commissioner-only fields in a clearly marked permission region.
screens.primaryDecision: Which class record needs an authorized correction?
remove: Public-looking gem/bust badges in the list
Portrait-first card browsing for repeated edits
screens.interaction: Filter then open a record; hidden traits stay out of public preview/share surfaces. Saving confirms the named recruit.
screens.compact: List to one category form, with commissioner-only notice attached to the relevant fields.
screens.difference: This editor prioritizes class visibility and privilege boundaries; roster correction prioritizes existing team membership.
unapprovedDependencies: No new reveal rules, hidden scouting exports or unsupported class-wide edits.
screens.title: Commissioner recruit editor

screens.composition: Named file workspace with a team tree on the left, roster grid center, selected field controls below; Save and Save as are file commands in the header.
screens.primaryDecision: Which reusable roster file am I creating or saving?
remove: Ambiguous Save that could overwrite an unknown destination
screens.interaction: Choose source, edit, then save to a named library destination. Leave prompts preserve the draft on Cancel.
screens.compact: Team picker to player grid to editor; file identity and dirty state remain visible.
screens.difference: File scope governs the whole workspace; no phase, readiness or accepted-result chrome.
unapprovedDependencies: New formats, binary Power Pros export and cloud conflict merging remain unapproved.
screens.title: Roster file studio

screens.composition: A broad roster table supports browsing; Compare pins two named players into aligned metric columns with their source files retained above each column.
screens.primaryDecision: Which player or source roster best fits my intended use?
remove: Radar art that hides actual metric values
screens.interaction: Select two records explicitly; metric groups switch together. Open player details without losing the comparison pair.
screens.compact: A shared metric label followed by A and B values on each row; no two shrinking profile pages.
screens.difference: Inspection and comparison rather than authoring; the viewer should not inherit the studio edit controls by default.
unapprovedDependencies: Cross-edition rating conversion and automatic roster recommendations are not approved.
screens.title: Roster browser and comparison

screens.composition: Library shelf of named classes leads to one class manifest. Recruit attributes use a table/editor workspace; Save, Share and Load into league are visibly separate command paths.
screens.primaryDecision: Save this reusable class or deliberately load it into a named league?
remove: One generic Publish command for three different outcomes
screens.interaction: Edit within the file; each outbound action states its actual destination and current visibility. Canceling Load returns to the unchanged draft.
screens.compact: Class list then recruit editor; Load opens its own destination review, not a tiny nested modal.
screens.difference: Class authoring is about reusable content and visibility; the live recruit editor is about a specific league correction.
unapprovedDependencies: New sharing permissions, marketplace metadata or non-destructive merge require approval.
screens.title: Recruiting class studio

screens.composition: A read-only manifest sits beside a concise source-to-destination transfer summary; outcome wording names library import versus league load as actually supported.
screens.primaryDecision: Do I want this shared file in the stated destination?
remove: Editable controls implying the source can be changed
screens.interaction: Preview recruits, then perform the supported import; success names what was created. Unauthorized destinations never appear available.
screens.compact: Transfer summary above a collapsible manifest; review and commit remain distinct.
screens.difference: A directional transfer review, not another library or recruitment page.
unapprovedDependencies: Duplicate detection, provenance signing and compatibility conversions need separate implementation.
screens.title: Shared class import

screens.composition: A compact class cover introduces a browsable prospect contact sheet; selected profile is read-only and a clear import link ends the visit.
screens.primaryDecision: Is this shared class worth exploring or importing?
screens.interaction: Browse profiles without mutation; open the supported import workflow as an explicit next step.
screens.compact: List with optional small portraits; profile opens full width and returns to the same place.
screens.difference: Public discovery rather than file editing: imagery can lead, but no live-league controls or hidden traits.
unapprovedDependencies: New ratings, download counters, public author identity and sharing modes require approval.
screens.title: Shared class showcase

screens.composition: There is no new designed destination. Replace the retired route with its accessible league hub; only a brief fallback names the current destination.
screens.primaryDecision: Continue to the current Matchday brief.
remove: Loading scene or new War Room branding
screens.interaction: Replace navigation history so Back does not loop; failed access uses the normal recovery state.
screens.compact: Same redirect; no separate phone design.
screens.difference: A compatibility route deliberately receives no new screen.
screens.title: Retired War Room link

screens.composition: One calm recovery page names the problem in plain language, offers an accessible hub when known, and always offers Dynasty selection. A small neutral diamond illustration is optional.
screens.primaryDecision: Choose a safe known destination.
remove: Raw route tokens or stack traces
Fake retry for permanently missing content
screens.interaction: Use one destination action; retry appears only for recoverable loading/network errors, not arbitrary 404s.
screens.compact: Short text and two full-width actions; no decorative scrolling page.
screens.difference: Recovery is a plain decision surface, not a disabled version of the normal dashboard.
screens.title: Page not found

screens.composition: Conference groups form one aligned standings ledger. The user team has a subtle row marker; any supported qualification boundary is labeled in the table itself.
screens.primaryDecision: Where does the program stand in the official race?
keep: Official record and games back where supported
screens.interaction: Choose conference, inspect a team, return to the same standings position.
screens.compact: Team, W-L and supported rank/GB remain primary; additional columns use metric presets.
screens.difference: A race table aligned by teams, unlike individual stat leaders or ranking opinions.
screens.title: League detail — Standings

screens.composition: A conference-organized directory of compact school nameplates fills the page. Selecting Compare opens a new two-program sheet with equal columns and matched metric periods.
screens.primaryDecision: Find a program or compare two named programs.
remove: Composite power score invented for visual impact
screens.interaction: Choose first and second program explicitly; compare is a separate route/state, with Swap and Clear.
screens.compact: Directory stays a list; comparison shows labeled A/B values per metric group.
screens.difference: A navigable program directory that changes composition only when comparison is requested.
unapprovedDependencies: Comparison state and return behavior need implementation; no new composite metric.
screens.title: League detail — Teams and comparison

screens.composition: A dated ranking release leads with week and source, followed by current rank, prior rank and movement in one full-width ordered list. New entrants use text, not a false delta.
screens.primaryDecision: How did this published ranking change?
remove: Standings record presented as ranking authority
screens.interaction: Switch published week only where snapshots exist; open the ranked program for context.
screens.compact: Rank, team and movement form one readable line with a secondary record line.
screens.difference: A published ordered snapshot rather than the competition standings table.
unapprovedDependencies: Historical ranking selection requires retained snapshots; absent methodology stays unexplained, not invented.
screens.title: League detail — Rankings

screens.composition: A league-wide discovery ledger prioritizes player identity, role, class rank when real, authorized known quality and availability. Team-specific spending controls are absent. A small view selector changes the existing combined/group scope.
screens.primaryDecision: Which prospect should I investigate next?
remove: Own-team resource meter on a league discovery screen
screens.interaction: Search/sort within authorized visible data, open a recruit dossier, then return to the same pool and selection. Recruiting actions belong to the player's authorized context.
screens.compact: Essential identity/position/status rows and metric presets; no huge prospect tiles or horizontally hidden fields.
screens.difference: Discovery across the league, contrasted with the own-board resource-allocation task; identical data does not justify identical controls.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No new recommendation algorithm, hidden-rating sort or public scouting disclosure.
screens.title: League detail — Prospects

screens.composition: Award categories form restrained cabinet headings. One selected honor gets recipient portrait, award name and season; other recipients remain a compact roll of honor below.
screens.primaryDecision: Inspect the actual recipient and achievement.
screens.interaction: Select category or recipient; open the actual player/season evidence. Do not trigger celebration for unawarded honors.
screens.compact: Award selector plus one featured recipient and roll of honor.
screens.difference: An achievement ceremony surface distinct from record lookup or raw leaders.
unapprovedDependencies: Original award silhouette/portrait assets; avoid EA trophies and licensed designs.
screens.title: League detail — Awards

screens.composition: A chronological season ledger shows year, champion and the few retained major outcomes. The main interaction is selecting a year; rich reading happens in Archive.
screens.primaryDecision: Which season should I open?
remove: Mini charts without consistent historical data
screens.interaction: Select a year to open its archive, not a separate competing history dashboard.
screens.compact: Stacked season rows with champion and Open year.
screens.difference: A concise index into Archive; it is not an additional archival content system.
screens.title: League detail — History

screens.composition: Date groups contain factual edit entries with actor, affected record and correction summary. Opening an entry reveals authorized before/after values directly below it.
screens.primaryDecision: What changed, and which record is affected?
remove: Audit data exposed as social news
screens.interaction: Expand one event inline or open its record; unavailable/restricted detail is labeled.
screens.compact: One event column; before and after stack with explicit labels.
screens.difference: A correction journal with precise provenance, separate from the public activity wire.
unapprovedDependencies: Do not reconstruct missing before/after values or expose private scouting through logs.
screens.title: League detail — Edits

screens.composition: Field view is a large readable diamond with actual player slots. Batting view is a nine-row order on a lineup card. Pitching view is named rotation roles and bullpen. Each has a small eligible bench drawer only when assigning.
screens.primaryDecision: Who belongs in this exact field, batting or pitching slot?
remove: Full roster spreadsheet always above field
screens.interaction: Select slot then eligible player; swap through explicit selectable actions. Drag may supplement but cannot replace this path.
screens.compact: Choose Field/Order/Pitching first; field uses labeled slots or accessible list, never unreadable miniatures.
screens.difference: Three baseball-specific spatial surfaces, not one table with a different heading.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No unsupported platoon/DH scenarios; companion changes do not claim to synchronize into Power Pros.
screens.title: Roster — Field, lineup and pitching

screens.composition: A full-width change ledger compares each player's recorded before and after values, grouped by metric preset. Selecting a row reveals a narrow explanation beneath it; top summary names the actual offseason.
screens.primaryDecision: What changed, and which player needs attention?
screens.interaction: Sort actual change or select athlete; switch hitting/pitching/common metric sets. Unknown history is labeled missing.
screens.compact: Player/change list first; one metric group per view; expanded explanation inline.
screens.difference: A before-and-after evidence sheet, not a roster browser or training minigame.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No new development prediction, training investment or potential model. Existing permissions remain authoritative.
screens.title: Roster — Development

screens.composition: A sports profile uses a large cel portrait, number and role on the left; exact roster attributes and supported season stats on the right. The action menu is small, separate and role-gated.
screens.primaryDecision: What can this rostered athlete do, and what am I allowed to change?
remove: Every possible mutation as a large primary button
Public profile controls that expose commissioner fields
screens.interaction: Navigate profile chapters; open a deliberate edit/action sheet only when permitted; closing restores the invoking roster row.
screens.compact: Single full-screen profile, identity at top and one data chapter.
screens.difference: A rostered-athlete card with known state; recruit dossier instead foregrounds uncertainty and relationship.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Public/own/opponent permissions require real response QA; no new mutable fields or export support.
screens.title: Player profile and authorized edit

screens.composition: Two or three athletes become columns in one aligned comparison matrix. Identity is a shallow header; traits, uncertainty, position fit and cost use identical row definitions. No separate cards with unequal content lengths.
screens.primaryDecision: Which candidate is the better use of this specific resource?
remove: Composite winner score without an approved formula
screens.interaction: Pin candidates, select metric preset and review differences; action opens a target-specific confirmation after comparison.
screens.compact: Two athletes and one metric group; a third requires explicit switch, not compressed type.
screens.difference: The only view designed around simultaneous side-by-side attribute evidence.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: No invented fit grade or knowledge ranges; hidden traits remain inaccessible even through sorting/export.
screens.title: Recruit comparison and action preview

screens.composition: Filtering is a compact labeled search form with live result count and active-filter chips. Visits uses an actual week/slot planner in its own mode. Action history is a plain chronological log. These are three tools, not one shared card grid.
screens.primaryDecision: Which targets match my criteria, or which actual visit slot can I use?
remove: Generic recap tiles inside filter panel
Mutations triggered by closing a search drawer
screens.interaction: Apply/reset filters explicitly; choose Visits to allocate a supported slot; choose History to inspect factual actions.
screens.compact: Full-width labeled form or week list; never a microscopic calendar.
screens.difference: Purpose changes determine form, planner or log; no permanent inspector for these utility tools.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Result count/visit timing must come from existing data; no invented scheduling constraints or controller support.
screens.title: Recruiting filters, visits and action history

screens.composition: A pending/disputed banner above submitted score and evidence; reviewed revision and submitter remain beside a compact confirm/dispute decision area. Team stat chapters occupy the main sheet.
screens.primaryDecision: Can I accept this exact report revision?
remove: A single optimistic green check for OCR, validity and approval
screens.interaction: Inspect evidence, choose confirm or provide dispute reason, then wait for server result. A changed revision requires deliberate rereview rather than silently accepting refreshed data.
screens.compact: Summary first, one stat chapter next, decision area reachable without losing review position.
screens.difference: This is a decision about another submission, not entry and not a final box score.
unapprovedDependencies: New automatic arbitration or evidence authentication is not implied.
screens.title: Pending report review and dispute

screens.composition: Final-state scoreboard over a full-width line score; paired team batting/pitching tables underneath; recap is a secondary chapter with provenance.
screens.primaryDecision: What happened, and which supported performance explains it?
remove: Invented pitch sequences for reported games
Zeros substituted to complete an empty table
screens.interaction: Read result, switch team/stat group, then open a player or available recap; return restores the fixture.
screens.compact: Selected team table with curated column groups; unavailable data gets a concise explicit state.
screens.difference: A permanent read-only record; no evidence-upload controls or approval buttons.
unapprovedDependencies: New derived advanced metrics and factual recap claims require suitable supplied data.
screens.title: Box score and game recap

screens.composition: A compact consequence sheet names the exact player(s), action and irreversible boundary. Before/after budget and roster state are aligned only where verified; Cancel and Confirm remain distinct.
screens.primaryDecision: Am I confirming the exact departure or retention action I intend?
remove: Generic 'Are you sure?' with no consequence
screens.interaction: Open from one decision, review current state, confirm explicitly; stale state rejection returns to the case instead of retrying blindly.
screens.compact: One readable consequence panel with top close; actions remain in content rather than global footer navigation.
screens.difference: A final transaction boundary, not another browseable profile.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Needs actual consequence data and mutation revalidation; no predicted outcome masquerading as certainty.
screens.title: Retention, declaration and finalization

screens.composition: A signed/outbid receipt lists confirmed outcomes with spend and roster impact where available. One featured signed athlete can appear above the list, but failures retain the same factual row treatment.
screens.primaryDecision: What actually happened to my bids?
remove: Automatic triumph language when no bid succeeded
screens.interaction: Select outcome for supported detail, then return to roster/bidding according to phase. No action repeats bidding.
screens.compact: Two explicit result groups and a full-width receipt; no carousel hiding losses.
screens.difference: A transaction outcome receipt, visibly calmer than bidding and shorter than a ceremony.
screens.unapprovedDependencies: Do not calculate unknown rival bids; spotlight is cosmetic and cannot create a signing or approved arrival ceremony.
screens.title: Walk-on auction results

screens.composition: Rows are teams/coaches; columns distinguish readiness, required report state and relevant blocker. The current advance operation sits directly above the matrix.
screens.primaryDecision: Whose unresolved obligation needs attention?
remove: Profile cards that hide missing obligations
screens.interaction: Open the exact missing report or permitted team detail from a row; no automatic message send.
screens.compact: Team rows become labeled status stacks; selecting one reveals obligations.
screens.difference: A cross-team readiness matrix inside the office, not a generic task-card collection.
unapprovedDependencies: Presence tracking and new reminders require explicit scope.
screens.title: Commissioner — Command center

screens.composition: A short list groups routine progression, correction and recovery. The chosen action replaces the list with preflight evidence, affected scope and a single execution control.
screens.primaryDecision: Is this specific operation currently permitted and understood?
remove: All mutations visible as equally inviting buttons
screens.interaction: Review one action, execute once, then inspect its actual operation state. Failed/blocked actions explain the server reason.
screens.compact: List to a full-screen operation review; back preserves selection without executing.
screens.difference: Procedural action review, unlike settings forms and historical audit browsing.
unapprovedDependencies: New force, rollback or exactly-once retry guarantees remain unapproved.
screens.title: Commissioner — Actions and recovery

screens.composition: Category navigation leads to a single settings form; current saved values and draft changes are visually separated, with phase-locked fields explained in place.
screens.primaryDecision: Which supported league setting should change?
remove: Settings mixed with immediate destructive actions
Sliders for unsupported or immutable rules
screens.interaction: Edit category, review valid differences, save; failed validation retains the draft and identifies the field.
screens.compact: Category picker and one form, without a long accordion of everything.
screens.difference: Persistent configuration rather than executing a one-time operation.
unapprovedDependencies: New rules, effective-date scheduling and role-transfer behavior require approval.
screens.title: Commissioner — Settings

screens.composition: Dense time-ordered rows with actor, operation and target; selecting a row opens a read-only evidence drawer. Filters reduce the ledger without changing its ordering.
screens.primaryDecision: Who changed this record, and what evidence is available?
screens.interaction: Filter by available fields, inspect record, copy nonsecret identifier. UI never turns absence of evidence into a success claim.
screens.compact: Rows show time/action first; event detail opens full width.
screens.difference: Forensic reading and traceability; unlike a current blocker queue it includes completed history.
unapprovedDependencies: New diff reconstruction, export formats or audit retention promises are unapproved.
screens.title: Commissioner — Audit

screens.composition: Compact invitation register with validity and permitted usage fields; selection exposes Copy or Revoke separately, with seat/coach assignment in its own area.
screens.primaryDecision: Which invitation should remain usable?
remove: Revoke adjacent to ordinary row selection
screens.interaction: Create or copy only through explicit actions; revoke names the selected invitation. No tokens in unrelated visual exports.
screens.compact: Named invitation list then actions; the token is deliberately revealed only where needed.
screens.difference: An access-management register, not marketing invitations or readiness tracking.
unapprovedDependencies: New invite expiry, seat limits or roles need backend support and approval.
screens.title: Commissioner — Invitations

screens.composition: Pending/disputed queue on the left; selected report evidence occupies the main area; decision controls bind to its displayed version. Accepted history is a separate filter/view.
screens.primaryDecision: Which report exception should I resolve now?
remove: Accepted and disputed scores styled identically
Bulk acceptance without full authorized review
screens.interaction: Select exception, inspect source and changed fields when available, then take the existing permitted action. Stale data blocks decision.
screens.compact: Queue to full decision sheet; return keeps filters and position.
screens.difference: League-wide triage leading into one report decision, distinct from a participant reviewing a single game.
unapprovedDependencies: New dispute rules, batch decisions and automated conflict resolution require approval.
screens.title: Commissioner — Reported results

screens.composition: Team rows align budget, recorded spending/obligations and available amount; selected team opens the existing allocation details and separately gated adjustment form.
screens.primaryDecision: What money is actually available, and does a correction need to be made?
remove: Invented transaction history from current totals
screens.interaction: Select team to inspect known accounting values; an edit names its precise field and scope, with server rejection preserved.
screens.compact: Labeled financial rows per team, then detail; keep numbers aligned.
screens.difference: An accounting inspection surface rather than a leaderboard or general editor.
unapprovedDependencies: Ledger reconstruction, currency conversion and new NIL policies remain unapproved.
screens.title: Commissioner — NIL

screens.composition: Week/team matrix provides coverage context; a ranked diagnostic list below links to exact affected fixtures. Warnings and blocking findings have separate text labels.
screens.primaryDecision: Which proven schedule problem must be inspected before advance?
screens.interaction: Choose a check to highlight affected rows/fixtures; repair appears only if already permitted.
screens.compact: Diagnostic list first; chosen check shows its team/week slice rather than the entire matrix.
screens.difference: A structural inspection view, while the schedule is a coach’s chronology of games.
unapprovedDependencies: New diagnostics, automatic repairs and calendar assumptions require specification.
screens.title: Commissioner — Schedule health

screens.composition: Entity-type selector above a searchable record list; one selected entity fills a categorized editor. Existing change history is adjacent but read-only until an authorized reversal is explicitly chosen.
screens.primaryDecision: Which named league entity and field should be corrected?
remove: Reversal portrayed as a harmless navigation action
screens.interaction: Select entity, edit category, review exact target and save. Preserve failed input and avoid implying bulk scope.
screens.compact: Record list to full form; breadcrumb retains entity and category.
screens.difference: Structural administration across entity types; dedicated roster/class editors optimize repeated player work.
unapprovedDependencies: Unsupported bulk mutation, reversible-history guarantees and new appearance controls need approval.
screens.title: Commissioner — League editor

screens.composition: Timestamped snapshot rows align season/phase/week and known scope; selection opens a comparison of documented coverage and actual restore restrictions, followed by guarded action.
screens.primaryDecision: Is this recovery point compatible and actually restorable?
remove: Green Restore button where restoration is blocked
screens.interaction: Inspect scope first; disabled restoration explains the real restriction. A request in flight is not a restored league.
screens.compact: Snapshot list to a full consequence review; avoid nested confirm dialogs.
screens.difference: Recovery evidence and compatibility, not a file marketplace or ordinary Save as.
unapprovedDependencies: Complete restore, consistent snapshot coverage and revision-safe recovery remain engineering gates; no new promise.
screens.title: Commissioner — Save states

screens.composition: Compact operation header with phase/week, server status and last known checkpoint; expand into a chronological status log only when useful or interrupted.
screens.primaryDecision: Is advance complete, still running, or in need of authorized recovery?
remove: Celebration before all required work finishes
screens.interaction: Allow safe navigation; return can inspect current operation. Recovery links carry the existing operation identity and do not imply safe automatic retry.
screens.compact: Status strip expands to one readable log panel.
screens.difference: A live process explanation, not a loading movie or a permanent audit ledger.
unapprovedDependencies: New cancellation, resumption guarantees and lease telemetry require verified endpoints.
screens.title: Advance progress and failure

screens.composition: A season cover names the final record and completed year. A deliberate reading sequence follows: results, actual honors, departing players and arrivals. Each chapter ends with its archive evidence link.
screens.primaryDecision: Review what the completed season meant and continue when ready.
screens.interaction: Next/previous chapter and contents list remain available; Exit returns without advancing league state.
screens.compact: One chapter per view with a persistent year label and clear contents control.
screens.difference: An end-of-season reading experience, while Archive remains the searchable reference.
unapprovedDependencies: Scrapbook export, new generated narration and share layouts remain unapproved dependencies.
screens.title: Season recap and program scrapbook

screens.composition: The shell supplies a small league/season/status band, then yields most space to each page's own composition. A top Menu opens grouped text destinations over the paused interface; preferences are a separate sheet.
screens.primaryDecision: Navigate to a named area or resume the current task.
remove: Global workspace plus mandatory sidebar on every screen
Bottom tab bar or unexplained icon-only destinations
screens.interaction: Open menu, choose group/destination, or Escape back to the exact invoking control; never discard dirty input silently.
screens.compact: A top Menu opens a full-screen named destination list; no bottom navigation.
screens.difference: The shell is a navigation layer, not the composition template for every screen.
unapprovedDependencies: Controller mapping, bookmarks, audio assets and persistent preference behavior require their own implementation/approval.
screens.title: Game menu, audio and system states

screens.composition: A small operation-specific sheet names source, destination and visibility; only fields needed for Save, Save as, Share or replacement appear.
screens.primaryDecision: What will this file action change, and where?
remove: Nested dialogs over an already narrow editor
screens.interaction: Each action has a precise verb; cancel returns to unchanged draft. Server outcome updates saved state only after success.
screens.compact: Full readable sheet with persistent filename/context; no nested scrolling.
screens.difference: Small bounded file operation, unlike full import review or authoring workspaces.
unapprovedDependencies: New overwrite detection, recovery storage and share permission modes are unapproved.
screens.title: File save, share, overwrite and unsaved changes
